A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block.
A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell.
A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code one 40-character screen row below the first cell.
A 256-byte table of bottom-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D60 writes the selected code one row below and one cell to the right of the first cell.

Load 18: low bytes for pointer entries 15–78 of the 81-entry split table. Paired with the high table, these encode $8DF1 through $AD71 in 128-byte steps modulo 65536, the row stride at $7F4A. They lie beyond the map’s 15 rows, the count at $7F4C.
